title: Prime maps and compatible sharp basic-chart homomorphisms from global sections
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space, $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative monoids with sharp stalks, and $P$ a fine sharp monoid, with additive notation and monoid-spectrum conventions as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For a monoid homomorphism $\varphi:P\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)$ put $\mathfrak m_x=\{p\in P:\varphi(p)_x\ne0\}$ and $V_a=\{x\in T:\varphi(a)_x=0\}$. Then $\mathcal A(V)$ is sharp for every open $V\subseteq T$, every $\mathfrak m_x$ is a prime ideal, and $h_\varphi(x)=\mathfrak m_x$ is a continuous map to $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$ with $h_\varphi^{-1}D(a)=V_a$. Moreover $\varphi(a)|_{V_a}=0$. Write $P_a=P-\mathbf N a$. There is a unique homomorphism $\lambda_a:P_a\to\mathcal A(V_a)$ extending restriction of $\varphi$, given by $\lambda_a(p-na)=\varphi(p)|_{V_a}$. It kills $P_a^\times$ and descends to $\theta_a:P_a/P_a^\times\to\mathcal A(V_a)$. Under the canonical section identifications of [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections], the $\theta_a$ commute with restrictions for every inclusion $D(b)\subseteq D(a)$ and agree after restriction to $D(a)\cap D(b)=D(a+b)$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99: construction of the prime map and extension to localizations; 3.1.1--3.1.4, p.98. Expands old parent Steps 1--2 and the descent/compatibility part of Step 3. No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric assertion.

proof.text: Use the sheaf and germ conventions of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. If $u+v=0$ in $\mathcal A(V)$, their germs satisfy $u_x+v_x=0$ for every $x\in V$. Thus $u_x$ is a unit, hence zero by sharpness. Equality of germs means that, for every $x$, $u$ and zero agree on some open neighborhood of $x$ in $V$. These neighborhoods cover $V$, so uniqueness in the sheaf axiom gives $u=0$. This also covers $V=\varnothing$ by the empty-cover sheaf axiom. Therefore $\mathcal A(V)$ is sharp for every open $V$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: For each $x$, let $f_x(p)=\varphi(p)_x$. The complement of $\mathfrak m_x$ contains $0$ and is closed under addition, since $f_x$ is a homomorphism. If $p\in\mathfrak m_x$ and $q\in P$, an equation $f_x(p+q)=0$ would make $f_x(p)$ a unit with inverse $f_x(q)$; sharpness would give $f_x(p)=0$, a contradiction. Thus $\mathfrak m_x+P\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$ and $0\notin\mathfrak m_x$. By the definition of prime ideal in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], $\mathfrak m_x$ is prime, including the possible empty ideal.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: By the definition of a germ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], $\varphi(a)_x=0$ holds exactly when $\varphi(a)$ is zero on some open neighborhood of $x$. Hence $V_a$ is the union of such neighborhoods and is open; their local equalities with zero glue to $\varphi(a)|_{V_a}=0$. From the definitions, $h_\varphi^{-1}D(a)=\{x:a\notin\mathfrak m_x\}=V_a$. Since the $D(a)$ form the spectrum topology basis in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], these open inverse images prove continuity.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: Fix $a$ and set $g(p)=\varphi(p)|_{V_a}$, so $g(a)=0$ by Step 3. The fine monoid $P$ embeds in $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. If $p-na=q-ma$ in $P_a$, then $p+ma=q+na$ in $P$; applying $g$ gives $g(p)=g(q)$. Thus $\lambda_a(p-na)=g(p)$ is well-defined. Addition of two representatives gives $\lambda_a((p-na)+(q-ma))=g(p+q)=g(p)+g(q)$, and $\lambda_a(0)=0$. It extends $g$. Any extension sends $-a$ to an additive inverse of $g(a)=0$, necessarily zero, and therefore sends every $p-na$ to $g(p)$. This proves uniqueness.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: For a unit $u\in P_a^\times$ choose $v$ with $u+v=0$. Then $\lambda_a(u)+\lambda_a(v)=0$; Step 1 gives $\lambda_a(u)=0$. If two elements of $P_a$ differ by addition of a unit, their images under $\lambda_a$ are consequently equal. The sharpening quotient in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] therefore gives a unique homomorphism $\theta_a:P_a/P_a^\times\to\mathcal A(V_a)$ with $\theta_a(\operatorname{cl}(p-na))=\varphi(p)|_{V_a}$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: For D(b) contained in D(a), inverse image under the continuous prime map gives V_b contained in V_a. Represent q in P_a by p/a^n and r in P_b by t/b^m with equal ambient values. Cross multiplication in P^gp and injectivity of P into P^gp give p*b^m=t*a^n in P. On V_b, both phi(b) and the restriction of phi(a) are 1. Applying the restricted numerator homomorphism therefore gives phi(p)|V_b=phi(t)|V_b. The fraction formulas for lambda_a and lambda_b, functoriality of restriction, and the quotient formulas for theta_a and theta_b give the required equality. This proves the ambient-fraction formulation directly from [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], without using the affine section identifications theorem.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed p.99; explicit sharp-stalk and localization calculation.

proof.text: For any prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, its ideal property and the closure of its complement show $a+b\notin\mathfrak p$ if and only if $a,b\notin\mathfrak p$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Hence $D(a)\cap D(b)=D(a+b)$, and Step 3 gives $V_a\cap V_b=V_{a+b}$. Apply Step 6 to the two inclusions $D(a+b)\subseteq D(a),D(b)$. Both restriction squares have the same map $\theta_{a+b}$ on the smaller chart, which proves agreement on the overlap.
